31s düşündü

The key distinction is between all FHA applications filed and applications that actually reached a lending decision. HMDA (the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act) records both, but they produce different denial rates.

The appropriate underlying source for calendar-year 2025 is the CFPB/FFIEC HMDA loan-level dataset, rather than FHA insurance claims or HUD fiscal-year loan statistics. The CFPB released the 2025 data on March 31, 2026. [CFPB: 2025 HMDA data release](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/about-us/newsroom/2025-hmda-data-on-mortgage-lending-now-available/?utm_source=chatgpt.com). Consumer Financial Protection Bureau +1

### 1\. Withdrawals compared with denials

The 2025 HMDA figures reported for FHA loans establish the following:

| Measure                          | 2025 count |
| -------------------------------- | ---------- |
| Total FHA applications           | 1,602,113  |
| Loans originated                 | 906,942    |
| Applications denied              | 265,894    |
| Denial share of all applications | 16.6%      |

These figures are from [Lender Register's 2025 FHA dataset](https://lenderregister.com/type/fha/?utm_source=chatgpt.com), which attributes its figures to the public FFIEC/CFPB HMDA records. Lender Register +1

One important qualification: the 16.6% figure uses all 1,602,113 applications, including withdrawals and files closed for incompleteness. It is not the conventional credit-decision denial rate.

HMDA distinguishes:

* Action 1: Loan originated.

* Action 2: Approved but not accepted.

* Action 3: Denied.

* Action 4: Withdrawn by applicant.

* Action 5: Closed for incompleteness.

These are separate outcomes, not interchangeable categories. [FFIEC/CFPB HMDA field definitions](https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/documentation/publications/loan-level-datasets/lar-data-fields?utm_source=chatgpt.com). HMDA Documentation +1

I cannot verify the nationwide FHA withdrawal count from the published aggregate table, so I would not invent a withdrawal percentage by subtracting other known outcomes.

There is, however, a useful independently reported comparison for FHA home-purchase applications:

| Outcome    | Count   | Share of applications |
| ---------- | ------- | --------------------- |
| Originated | 640,557 | 70.6%                 |
| Denied     | 96,258  | 10.6%                 |
| Withdrawn  | 141,198 | 15.55%                |

Source: [2025 HMDA FHA home-purchase analysis](https://scarpero.com/why-va-purchase-loans-are-denied/?utm_source=chatgpt.com). Carlos Scarpero

This is a purchase-only subset, not the entire FHA market. It nevertheless establishes that withdrawals were substantially more common than denials in that subset: approximately 1.47 withdrawals for every denial.

### 2\. Why do published FHA denial rates range from 13% to 22%?

The difference is principally about the population being measured and the denominator used.

Here are the important distinctions.

A. Home purchases versus all loan purposes

The approximately 13% figure can be reproduced using FHA home-purchase applications and a restricted decision denominator.

The 2025 purchase-only analysis reports:

* 96,258 denials.

* 640,557 originations.

* 13.06% denial rate when calculated as:

\\frac{96,258}{96,258+640,557}=13.06\\%

This excludes approved-but-not-accepted applications from the denominator.

The approximately 22% figure covers FHA applications across loan purposes, including:

* Home purchases.

* Refinancing.

* Cash-out refinancing.

* Home improvement.

* Other purposes.

Refinancing and other loan purposes can have different applicant and underwriting profiles. Carlos Scarpero +1

B. Different definitions of the decision denominator

HMDA permits several possible calculations:

| Calculation                                                | Included outcomes  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| Denials / (originations + denials)                         | Actions 1 and 3    |
| Denials / (originations + approved-not-accepted + denials) | Actions 1, 2 and 3 |
| Denials / all applications                                 | Actions 1–5        |

The second is the more useful conventional measure of the share of applications reaching a credit decision that were denied.

The first excludes approved-but-not-accepted applications. The third includes withdrawals and incomplete files, which are not credit decisions.

The FFIEC explains these categories in its [HMDA data definitions](https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/documentation/publications/loan-level-datasets/lar-data-fields?utm_source=chatgpt.com). HMDA Documentation +1

C. Forward mortgages versus reverse mortgages

There is another important data-cleaning issue.

An earlier 2025 FHA calculation reported a 21.7% denial rate using 1,217,297 decisioned applications. That universe included 29,691 reverse-mortgage (HECM) records.

After excluding those records, the calculation became:

\\frac{262,250}{1,187,606}=22.08\\%

Rounded, that is 22.1%.

Source: [FinanceRateCalc – 2025 FHA denial rate and correction history](https://financeratecalc.com/how-often-are-fha-loans-denied.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com). FinanceRateCalc

D. Calendar-year data versus other reporting periods

HMDA figures represent calendar-year lending activity. HUD's FHA program reports may use fiscal-year periods and different populations, such as insured originations rather than applications.

Those figures should not be treated as interchangeable.

HUD's [FHA market-share reports](https://www.hud.gov/hud-partners/single-family-mortgage-market-share?utm_source=chatgpt.com) provide a separate source for FHA program activity. hud.gov

### Bottom line

I would use the following figures when presenting 2025 FHA lending statistics:

| Statistic                                             | Figure               | What it measures                                                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| FHA denial rate, broad decisioned universe            | 22.1%                | All forward FHA purposes; actions 1–3                                       |
| FHA denial rate, purchase-only restricted denominator | 13.06%               | Purchase applications; originations plus denials                            |
| FHA denial share of all applications                  | 16.6%                | All applications, including withdrawals and incomplete files                |
| FHA withdrawal share                                  | Not established here | Requires the nationwide action-4 count and an explicitly stated denominator |

The central point is that 13% and 22% are not necessarily contradictory estimates of the same statistic. They reflect different loan-purpose populations and, importantly, different denominator conventions.

For a report or formal comparison, I would quote 22.1% as the broad 2025 FHA forward-mortgage decisioned-application denial rate, and clearly label the 13.06% figure as purchase-only.

I would also leave the nationwide withdrawal percentage unquoted until the action-4 count has been independently extracted from the 2025 HMDA file. That avoids presenting an unsupported figure as a federal statistic.
